quotes.text: Shopping malls epitomise the top of the supply chain. These mammoth, glorious, mega-palaces of consumption are filled to the brim with stuff, objects, products, goods, material artefacts for sale. They make me think about the fact that every single item there has, in the making of it, been touched by the bare hands of someone in impoverished conditions, somewhere, very far away.
quotes.speaker: Persis Jadé Maravala (ZU-UK)
quotes.source: LIFT Festival, 'LIFTing the curtain on Radio Ghost' (interview, 4 Aug 2022; archived copy)

quotes.text: It’s a Shinto belief that everything has a spirit, and I was interested in unlocking these ‘ghosts’ that betoken the hidden stories of the supply chain.
quotes.speaker: Persis Jadé Maravala (ZU-UK)
quotes.source: LIFT Festival, 'LIFTing the curtain on Radio Ghost' (interview, 4 Aug 2022; archived copy)

quotes.text: Ultimately, we wanted to prompt responses to questions about society, consumerism and loneliness. To make a game that would be played out against the ordinary backdrop of a shopping mall but in which the familiar would turn hauntingly strange.

quotes.source: LIFT Festival, 'LIFTing the curtain on Radio Ghost' (interview, 4 Aug 2022; archived copy)

quotes.text: But the question remains – what do we do with the knowledge of the suffering of others? A simple thing that the game suggests is that all we are asking for is informed consumer decision-making – the right to know.

quotes.source: LIFT Festival, 'LIFTing the curtain on Radio Ghost' (interview, 4 Aug 2022; archived copy)

quotes.text: It is about learning to put the blame where it belongs and how it is that certain things came to be in our hands, delivered to us by the hands of ghosts… and that no matter how hard you dust, you’ll not find their fingerprints.

title: Raster und Spectrum
summary: Raster und Spectrum is an onchain abstract real-time animation that can play on any device, shown by Nguyen Wahed in the Zero 10 section of Art Basel Miami Beach 2025. Two brushes — a raster of white lines on black and a spectrum that continuously cycles through hues — cross the screen in one of eight directions and return when they meet an edge.

title: Re: cite, member, sist
summary: Re: cite, member, sist is a site-specific installation with textile, 4-channel sound and found material, commissioned for Colomboscope 2026 (Rhythm Alliances) and shown at Colpetty Town House, Colombo. According to the festival publication it combines layered cyanotypes, shadow drawings referencing early illustrations of Portuguese colonial exploits, tracings of the artist's grandmother's embroidery patterns on cushions, curtains and household objects, and sound recordings of ocean tides and dialogues with her aunt. It draws on the artist's family's Goan history and her grandmother's migration from Bardez to Karachi.
summary_by: editorial summary written from the sources; not the artist's words

title: Reality Looks Back
summary: A 21-minute dome documentary, world-premiered in the IDFA DocLab Competition for Immersive Non-Fiction in 2025 and shown in the DocLab Exhibition and at the Planetarium, directed by Anne Jeppesen with co-director Omid Zarei (Superposition XR Studio). Jeppesen's narration moves through quantum observation, split déjà vu, parallel realities and the death of her elderly hamster Oliver, over documentary footage processed into Gaussian splats. The work began as an audio piece made in the YASS! mentorship programme (Lucia Festival / Radio Papesse), premiered in Florence in 2024.
summary_by: editorial summary written from the sources; not the artist's words

title: Regular Animals
summary: Regular Animals is an installation of autonomous robot dogs fitted with hyper-realistic silicone heads of figures including Andy Warhol, Pablo Picasso, Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, Jeff Bezos and Beeple himself, which move around a glass-walled pen using LIDAR to avoid each other. The robots take pictures of their surroundings, reinterpret them with AI in the style associated with each character, and print them out of their rear; some of the prints carry QR codes to claim NFTs. It was first shown at Art Basel Miami Beach's Zero 10 section in December 2025 and later at the Neue Nationalgalerie, Berlin, in 2026.
summary_by: editorial summary written from the sources; not the artist's words

title: REPETAE
summary: A series of language artworks combining AI-generated text, code-based visuals sketched in p5.js, and digitally looped and layered spoken word, presented as standalone works and longer interconnected cycles built around repetition. Parts include a browser-based piece that generates a new line of poetry every few minutes from the mantra WORDS CAN COMMUNICATE BEYOND WORDS. It received a Prix Ars Electronica 2024 Award of Distinction (AI in ART) and was shown as REPETAE: Again, Again at the Lentos Museum, Linz.
summary_by: editorial summary written from the sources; not the artist's words

quotes.text: It has to do with challenging the notion that creativity is solely about originality or "first-ness," and emphasizes how innovation comes from revisiting, reimagining and reinventing the familiar.
quotes.speaker: Sasha Stiles
quotes.source: Flaunt — Sasha Stiles' 'REPETAE' | The Seduction and Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence

quotes.text: So much dialogue around creative AI has to do with appropriation, copying, imitation, and how such "repetition" can never be authentic. With REPETAE, I want to probe how repeating patterns, words and ideas are at the heart of both human and machine creativity—how "again-ness" can yield fresh perspectives, lead to innovation and epiphany.
quotes.speaker: Sasha Stiles
quotes.source: Flaunt — Sasha Stiles' 'REPETAE' | The Seduction and Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence

quotes.text: The most accurate way I can describe the collaboration between me and Technelegy is that together we become a third voice that doesn't exist without us. The poems we write together can't be written entirely by an autonomous system, and they also cannot be written entirely by an analog human mind.
quotes.speaker: Sasha Stiles
quotes.source: Flaunt — Sasha Stiles' 'REPETAE' | The Seduction and Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence

quotes.text: At its core, REPETAE seeks to illuminate how meaning accrues through repetition, and how repetition shapes our engagement with art and the world around us.

quotes.text: The project invites consideration of the spatial, temporal, and philosophical dimensions of repetition as reinvention, and aims to prompt deeper reflections on the role of algorithm in the deeply human act of making art.

title: Requiem for an Exit
summary: An installation centred on a four-metre-tall armless robotic figure on a steel and hydraulic structure, whose hyperrealistic face is a projected animation built from a motion-capture recording of Thomas Kvam. In a darkened room with multichannel sound, the robot delivers a monologue written by the artists and voiced with AI speech synthesis, tracing genocide through human history from the disappearance of the Neanderthals; there is no interactivity. First shown at Meta.Morf 2024 in Trondheim (co-produced by TEKS); Golden Nica, New Animation Art, Prix Ars Electronica 2025.
summary_by: editorial summary written from the sources; not the artist's words

sources.title: Words as Weapons – Ars Electronica Blog (interview)

quotes.text: What interests us is what we inherit, not just genetically, but symbolically and ethically. The question is: What do we carry forward—consciously or not? The monologue doesn’t answer—it destabilizes. It turns the body into an archive and asks us to listen.
quotes.speaker: Thomas Kvam
quotes.source: Ars Electronica Blog, 'Words as Weapons' (Katia Kreuzhuber), 7 July 2025

quotes.text: Some might interpret this as biopolitical determinism, but our intention is quite the opposite—to dismantle the idea of simple explanations. There is no app against evil.
quotes.speaker: Frode Oldereid
quotes.source: Ars Electronica Blog, 'Words as Weapons' (Katia Kreuzhuber), 7 July 2025

quotes.text: Rather than asking who we are, the work asks how many times we will be the same. It confronts repetition itself—those inherited patterns looping through history. But within that cycle lies a question—or perhaps an opening: Can we become something other than what we were?
quotes.speaker: Frode Oldereid
quotes.source: Ars Electronica Blog, 'Words as Weapons' (Katia Kreuzhuber), 7 July 2025

quotes.text: And we are easily deceived: a few words in the right order, a sigh in the right place—and we think we’re talking to something alive. We exploit that weakness. It’s an existential question in technological disguise.
quotes.speaker: Thomas Kvam
quotes.source: Ars Electronica Blog, 'Words as Weapons' (Katia Kreuzhuber), 7 July 2025

quotes.text: Like demagogues throughout history, it wields rhetoric as a tool of influence, its words more potent than any physical gestures.
quotes.speaker: Frode Oldereid & Thomas Kvam
quotes.source: Requiem for an Exit (2024), artists' website

title: Rhythmic Ramp
summary: Rhythmic Ramp (Rampa rítmica) is a site-specific work by Cevdet Erek on the external ramp of Oscar Niemeyer's Ciccillo Matarazzo Pavilion at the 36th Bienal de São Paulo, the ramp that connects the exhibition's floors. It combines sonic and geometric elements placed along the ramp. Its sound includes rhythmic patterns drawn from music undergrounds in Istanbul and from São Paulo's vernacular rhythms, and visitors and passersby meet it as they go up and down the ramp.

title: Ri-lancia Luigi Broglio (Re-launching Luigi Broglio)
summary: Ri-lancia Luigi Broglio is a 33-minute 360° VR film directed by Vincenzo Cavallo, staged like a theatre piece, about Luigi Broglio, who launched Italy into space from the San Marco sea platform off Kenya in the 1960s. The viewer watches a confrontation between Broglio and a journalist in the abandoned command centre, with flashbacks to the African expedition, an encounter with Enrico Mattei and a near-diplomatic crisis with President Nasser. It was supported by Biennale College Cinema Immersive and shown out of competition at Venice Immersive 2025.
summary_by: editorial summary written from the sources; not the artist's words

title: Résonances
summary: Résonances is an interactive installation in which a visitor's gestures return as a visual and sound echo: earlier actions resurface and overlap with present ones, so the visitor can choreograph the present on top of their own past. It was unveiled in December 2021 in the CORPS DATA exhibition at Îlot Balmoral in Montreal with ELEKTRA, and shown at the 6th International Digital Art Biennial (BIAN) at Arsenal Contemporary Art Montreal; an outdoor edition was presented at i Light Singapore 2023 and Future Media FEST 2024 in Taipei.
summary_by: editorial summary written from the sources; not the artist's words

title: Sange Khara [Hard Stone]
summary: Sange Khara [Hard Stone] is an installation developed for the 36th Bienal de São Paulo, anchored by a looping 16mm film of desert and oasis landscapes and figures drawn from cinematic references. Visitors sit or lie down under a tent-like canopy of melhifa cloth, a fabric worn by women in the Sahara, in a scenography based on nomadic structures of southern Morocco, surrounded by sound and light. It is a chapter of Hida's ongoing project Le Voyage du Phénix.
summary_by: editorial summary written from the sources; not the artist's words

quotes.text: I’ve always been drawn to building spaces rather than objects. I’m interested in how we can experience art through the body—through rest, slowness, or stillness. In Sangeh Khara, viewers lie down under a canopy of melhifa fabric, surrounded by sound and light. The installation echoes nomadic architecture in the oases, where shade is essential. I wanted to offer a space that envelops the viewer—a place to breathe, to see differently.
quotes.speaker: Laila Hida
quotes.source: ART AFRICA Magazine, 'Laila Hida: Sensing the Desert, Reimagining the Image' (interview by Brendon Bell-Roberts)

quotes.text: What connects them is a shared question: how do we free the desert from the Orientalist image that has defined it for centuries? My films respond to those inherited representations through fragments, circular narratives, and lived experiences that resist the linear gaze of colonial storytelling.
quotes.speaker: Laila Hida
quotes.source: ART AFRICA Magazine, 'Laila Hida: Sensing the Desert, Reimagining the Image' (interview by Brendon Bell-Roberts)

quotes.text: Choosing slowness and intimacy becomes an act of resistance. My work doesn’t announce messages; it asks questions. The poetic allows me to speak about violence or history in ways that remain human, emotional, and open.
quotes.speaker: Laila Hida
quotes.source: ART AFRICA Magazine, 'Laila Hida: Sensing the Desert, Reimagining the Image' (interview by Brendon Bell-Roberts)

quotes.text: For Sangeh Khara, it felt important to work within a material economy—one that reflects the ecology of the desert itself. The fragility of film mirrors the fragility of the landscapes I’m filming.
quotes.speaker: Laila Hida
quotes.source: ART AFRICA Magazine, 'Laila Hida: Sensing the Desert, Reimagining the Image' (interview by Brendon Bell-Roberts)

quotes.text: Sangeh Khara speaks to how we inhabit the world together, how materials and images migrate and find new forms elsewhere.
quotes.speaker: Laila Hida
quotes.source: ART AFRICA Magazine, 'Laila Hida: Sensing the Desert, Reimagining the Image' (interview by Brendon Bell-Roberts)

title: Satan in America and Other Invisible Evils: Experiments in Public Sculpture (Witches 1–3)
summary: Three witch figures in an installation shown at the Whitney Biennial 2026 that draws on scenes from American history, from the Salem witch trials to Abraham Lincoln's birth near Hodgenville, Kentucky. The witches' bodies are built from open-source medical 3D CT scans of human bodies, and two Salem villagers nearby are built from character models taken from the video game Doom. Visitors walk among figures mounted on metal poles alongside the artist's Symbolic Birth Cabin Unit and two demon figures.
summary_by: editorial summary written from the sources; not the artist's words

quotes.text: This installation is really about insides and outsides and us versus them and hysteria and agony. I'm not trying to talk about witchcraft, the spiritual practice. I'm more trying to evoke the hysteria or the sense of fear or the possible parallels between Salem and now.
quotes.speaker: Isabelle Frances McGuire
quotes.source: Whitney Biennial 2026 audio guide, stop 520

quotes.text: It kind of also works like how science fiction is about the future, but it's normally about the present. So mine is a parallel world using these symbols, from the well of information and the well of free public virtual world.
quotes.speaker: Isabelle Frances McGuire
quotes.source: Whitney Biennial 2026 audio guide, stop 520

quotes.text: Something from a game space: the gift from the game Doom is a hell game space. So you kind of understand, very simply and easily, what this hell space might be like because we have a cultural similarity. And I think that's important for a sculptural conversation, which historically, sculptures are about, or have modeled, myths.
quotes.speaker: Isabelle Frances McGuire
quotes.source: Whitney Biennial 2026 audio guide, stop 520

title: Screen Melancholy
summary: Screen Melancholy (2026) is a video installation by Li Yi-Fan, presented by the Taipei Fine Arts Museum as Taiwan's collateral event at the 61st Venice Biennale in the Palazzo delle Prigioni, curated by Raphael Fonseca. In the video, Li performs a monologue through a game-engine digital character in the tone of an online tutorial, addressing subscription-based image software and AI-generated images. Large sculptures of fragmented limbs are placed throughout the space; visitors can sit on them and charge their phones from chargers built into the sculptures.
summary_by: editorial summary written from the sources; not the artist's words

quotes.text: Within the counterbalance of exhaustion, tension and collision, a narrative slowly emerges. In contemporary image production, artists inevitably rely on lots of different software tools. Some are open-source and free, while others are highly commercial. Each choice represents a different possibility for expression, but also has its own limitations and controls. I move among these systems, trying to grasp the subtle relationship of dependence and resistance between artists and contemporary tools. Through this process, using these image production techniques, I contemplate the state of humankind in relation to technological media.
quotes.speaker: Li Yi-Fan
quotes.source: Taipei Fine Arts Museum announcement, via photography-now.com, 'Screen Melancholy'

quotes.text: Is what you see on your phone truly what you want to see, or is it just pushed to you? When you realize everything is being spoon-fed, that helplessness is the truest form of melancholy

title: Skeleton of the Glorious
summary: Skeleton of the Glorious is a light installation by Khalid Zahid in the gardens of the King Abdulaziz Historical Center for Noor Riyadh 2025. It is a hollow, wireframe-like structure based on Al-Masmak Fort, the adobe and clay citadel of old Riyadh. It is lit from within, so the inner form is visible while the exterior falls into shadow.

title: SKY/WORLD DEATH/WORLD
summary: A two-part Whitney artport commission for the Sunrise/Sunset series (Dec 2022–Apr 2023) that played on whitney.org at sunrise and sunset in New York. SKY/WORLD pairs game-engine animations of dawn, drawing on the Haudenosaunee story of Sky Woman, with the question "Who benefits from your burnout?"; DEATH/WORLD pairs abstract visuals and video of the artist recovered from the Internet Archive with "What is made bright by the loss of your light?". title: SMOG SEASON
summary: SMOG SEASON is an installation of 80 cigarette packs mounted on 5 motor-driven circular bases, using Bangkok PM 2.5 air-pollution data and the cigarette-equivalence figure from Berkeley Earth (one cigarette per 22 micrograms per cubic meter per day). Visitors scan a QR code, choose a smoke level on their smartphone and hold it to a light sensor; the bases spin and lights blink at 18 FPS so the cigarette-label pictures appear animated, while an LED display shows the date, time and PM 2.5 value. It received an Honorary Mention in Prix Ars Electronica 2023 (New Animation Art).

If we count the problem of PM 2.5 as a season, it would be a very bad monsoon that people must suffer and endure to pass.

quotes.source: Witaya Junma, artist website, 'Smog Season'

quotes.text: "What do we breathe in?" The work wishes to expand on the point of PM 2.5 in Thailand. It is expanding into a chronic problem that is not solved. quotes.speaker: Witaya Junma
quotes.source: Witaya Junma, artist website, 'Smog Season'

title: Smoke and Mirrors
summary: A 4m30s data animation based on NASA's Blue Marble photograph: a counter shows atmospheric methane in parts per billion from 1970 to the present while the rotating globe fills with pink smoke, and advertising slogans from the oil industry (e.g. "Out to clean the air", "Unsettled Science", "Doomsday is cancelled") appear across the screen at their dates. It is set to the song "Oh My Heart" and was produced with the studio Parliament, using NOAA, NASA and EEA data. It received the Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica (New Animation Art) in 2024 and has been shown as a video and in exhibitions.
summary_by: editorial summary written from the sources; not the artist's words

quotes.source: Statement of Intent, Smoke and Mirrors (beatiewolfe.com)

quotes.text: Realising that a crucial piece of the climate puzzle (how we got to this critical point) has been the fossil fuel industry’s response to the emerging environmental awareness of the 1970s, and that methane emissions (30 times more potent than carbon for trapping heat) are increasingly linked with that industry, I wanted to illuminate this key parallel timeline.
quotes.speaker: Beatie Wolfe
quotes.source: Statement of Intent, Smoke and Mirrors (beatiewolfe.com)

quotes.text: The ‘smoke and mirrors’ tactics of the big oil industry (and many political bodies and corporations) are so hard to grasp, which leaves a lot of people feeling disempowered, so I wanted this project to help make this slippery reality visible and tangible.

title: Soft Collision
summary: Soft Collision is a deformable pneumatic silicone membrane with embedded sensors that wraps a UR5 industrial robot arm. A person physically pushes and guides the arm to program its movement, then adjusts its trajectory through the sensors while it replays; air chambers inflate in short bursts as feedback. It was developed in the VOJEXT S+T+ARTS residency and shown with a performer.

title: Solwata
summary: Solwata is a 25-minute mixed reality installation, narrated by Mark Ruffalo, about rising seas and planned relocation in the Solomon Islands, co-produced by Human Rights Watch, Agog: The Immersive Media Institute and NowHere Media and shown in Venice Immersive 2026. Participants interact with water and artifacts and, through 360° video, Gaussian splats and 3D animation, join community members Martha, Francis and Lawrence. It was made with residents of Walande, Ngongosila and Kwai.

quotes.text: It forces a reckoning: what is your position in this? What will you do when these changes arrive at your door? That’s the question we want audiences to sit with.
quotes.speaker: Felix Gaedtke, Gayatri Parameswaran (NowHere Media)
quotes.source: La Biennale di Venezia, Venice Immersive 2026 — Main Creators' Statement (NowHere Media - Felix Gaedtke, Gayatri Parameswaran)

quotes.text: One moment from our trip stays with us – diving underwater to see the remains of the submerged island of Walande, which was once home to a thriving community, now entirely displaced due to rising sea levels. It was sobering, and struck us deeply: this could be all our futures.
quotes.speaker: Felix Gaedtke, Gayatri Parameswaran (NowHere Media)

title: Songs for dying
summary: A 30-minute HD film with installation, co-commissioned by the 13th Gwangju Biennale, Kunsthall Trondheim and the Han Nefkens Foundation, narrated by the voice of a sea turtle, that combines footage around the death and funeral of the artist's grandfather with Jeju Island's shamanic rituals commemorating the 1948 uprising and the 2020 pro-democracy protests in Thailand. In the installation the video is accompanied by a diorama figure of gravel, moss, clay, modelled roots and banana leaves, with hands cast from the grandfather's. It opened at Kunsthall Trondheim in February 2021 and was shown at the Gwangju Biennale the same year.

It presents recordings, interviews and performance videos from Singing Wells' archive of East African music. Singing Wells was founded in 2011 by Nairobi's Ketebul Music and London's Abubilla Music, and travels to villages with a mobile recording studio.

title: Speak Slowly and It Will Become a Song
summary: Speak Slowly and It Will Become a Song (2025) is an outdoor sound installation on the Lawn Square of the Aichi Prefectural Ceramic Museum in Seto, commissioned for the performing arts programme of Aichi Triennale 2025. Visitors walk the lawn wearing headphones; with high-resolution GPS and three-dimensional audio, the sounds change with the visitor's movement. The material includes folk songs and life songs improvised by local women, voices and interviews from Seto, and sounds of clay, water, fire and vegetation, with surrounding background sound that the artist says was interpreted by AI.

title: Spray and Pray
summary: Spray and Pray is a 15-minute speculative animated documentary in Bulgarian about 'mushroom websites', automatically generated news sites that earn advertising revenue by spreading disinformation. Its CGI characters are built from anonymised research data and performed roles and speak with synthetic voices; a mushroom figure speaks only in headlines collected from such sites, which were also analysed with Bulgarian-language machine-learning models. It premiered at Visions du Réel in 2026 and is shown in the Bulgarian Pavilion at the 2026 Venice Biennale.

quotes.source: ArtReview, Venice Biennale: Artist Q&As (Bulgaria), 28 May 2026

quotes.text: Spray and Pray works within these ‘minor’ zones – the background infrastructures, automated protocols and algorithmically amplified signals that shape collective imagination. Rather than focusing on visible events, the film examines the conditions that make certain narratives persuasive.

quotes.source: ArtReview, Venice Biennale: Artist Q&As (Bulgaria), 28 May 2026

quotes.text: The film treats their outputs not as evidence, but as unstable readings, surfaces that expose the limits, biases, and ambiguities of automated interpretation.

title: Stained
summary: A CGI short film set in Mojo, a fictional future in which Black culture transforms American landscapes. It follows Demetrius, a tea master in the Crimson Needles gang, which uses colored flora to mark territory, as he relives being reprimanded for his fascination with a forbidden blue plant. Credits list music by Nathan Buttel and Jeremy Kamal and AI creative direction by Case Miller; it received a Prix Ars Electronica 2024 Award of Distinction in New Animation Art.

quotes.source: Ars Electronica Archive — Stained (Prix Ars Electronica 2024)

quotes.source: Ars Electronica Archive — Stained (Prix Ars Electronica 2024)

title: Still Life: Icon and Fetish (manifestation 1)
summary: A grid of archival prints on canvas (54 x 54 inches) made with AI models trained on a dataset of European floral still-life paintings. The central image comes from a model trained slowly on whole paintings; the surrounding images come from a model trained quickly on randomly cropped details of the same paintings. It was shown in custom frames in Agrawal's solo exhibition EXO-stential: AI Musings on the Posthuman at Emami Art, Kolkata, in September 2021; a related video work is titled (Un)Still Life.
summary_by: editorial summary written from the sources; not the artist's words

sources.title: Take on Art, 'Re-cognizing AI Art: Looking Back, Forward'

quotes.text: Positing the question, can machines be taught aesthetics, here the artist trains a machine to look at thousands of still-life paintings, some in their entirety, and some in their details, to try and guide a machine to learn both composition and the painterly nuances of aesthetic.
quotes.speaker: Harshit Agrawal
quotes.source: (Un)Still Life- Icon and Fetish, artist's website

quotes.text: In any painting what is the relation of the part (as fetish) to the whole (as icon)? How can one teach a computer compositional structure and painterly texture? This work tries to start poking into these set of questions.
quotes.speaker: Harshit Agrawal
quotes.source: (Un)Still Life- Icon and Fetish, artist's website (archival print on canvas)

quotes.text: For the second AI, the learning rate is kept fast since the attempt is for the machine to learn abstracted visuals from the dataset - the painterly as opposed to the compositional of the first. Thus, experimenting with both treatments of the dataset and the AI learning process, a new study in aesthetics of icon and fetish emerges.
quotes.speaker: Harshit Agrawal
quotes.source: STIR, 'Harshit Agrawal's Exo-stential is India's first solo artificial intelligence art show' (interview by Rahul Kumar), 5 October 2021

title: Subnormal Europe
summary: A 60-minute music theatre piece commissioned by the City of Munich for the Münchener Biennale and co-produced with the ZKM Hertz-Lab, performed by contralto Noa Frenkel and sound engineer Sebastian Schottke in an installation of three large screens, nine loudspeakers, MIDI-DMX lighting and a wooden cube. title: Taala Village
summary: Taala Village ('Village of Rhythms') is a pixel-art video game newly commissioned for Colomboscope 2026 (Rhythm Alliances). Players move through a virtual island where actions are accompanied by sounds of Sri Lankan instruments such as the thalampata, drums and conch shells, and meet a speculative community that worships fire and practises rituals, legends and folklore, with settings drawn from kovils, Buddhist temples and village habitats.

title: TALK SHOW
summary: TALK SHOW is a 27-minute color film with sound, the final part of Jordan Strafer's Loophole trilogy, shown in a dark gallery with armchairs at the Whitney Biennial 2026. It unfolds across two periods: the turn of the millennium, shot in color (including a reenactment of John F. Kennedy Jr.'s last radio exchange before his 1999 plane crash), and the afterlife, shot in black and white. Most of the film is a daytime talk show in which a host questions a panel of men who confess to rapes while the women they raped watch from backstage; the screenplay draws on news footage and self-help media.

title: Templo da água: rio Tietê
summary: A circular sound installation in which long copper flutes connected to glass bulbs are suspended and moved by a mechanical system that dips them into a basin of water; the filling and emptying of the bulbs pushes air through the tubes and makes them sound. The water was collected from the upper Tietê River, is kept oxygenated during the show and was to be returned to the river afterwards. Visitors sit on benches arranged around the basin and listen; at the 36th Bienal de São Paulo the work was also activated by performances by Vásquez and Esmeralda Ramírez (Werebere group).

title: The Echinoidea Future – Adriatic Sensing

title: The Great Orator
summary: The Great Orator is a 40-minute nonlinear VR story world by Daniel Ernst (The Shoebox Diorama) about a TV preacher whose consciousness lives on as an AI after her death. The visitor explores spaces such as a preserved house, a mainframe holding her followers' shared consciousness and an infinite parking lot, and points a hand at objects to receive her memories, which are generated from the visitor's interaction, random Internet input and live news feeds and differ on each visit. It premiered at Venice Immersive 2025.

title: The Innocence of Unknowing
summary: The Innocence of Unknowing is an AI archival project, two-channel essay film and live performance examining U.S. news media coverage of mass shootings since the 1960s, studying footage of people retreating. In the performance the artists question an AI model, trained on humanities texts, about its readings of the archive footage, shown alongside computer-vision analyses such as object and pose detection. It had its world premiere at Tribeca Immersive 2025 ('In Search of Us').

title: The Maw Of
summary: A web-based animation with an augmented-reality layer, commissioned for the Whitney Museum's artport and co-commissioned by KW Institute for Contemporary Art, Berlin. In the browser, a ghostly female figure drawn in a manga style moves through layers of interfaces, elements of whitney.org, a graph of the nervous system, a web console, parental-guidance alerts and military infrared imagery; scanning an on-screen QR code opens an AR layer on the viewer's phone that adds text and moves the figure out of the browser onto the device. A site-specific version (five-channel video, LED screens, sculpture and a hand-tracking VR environment) was shown 15–18 September 2022 at the Tieranatomisches Theater, Berlin.

title: The Oracle: Ritual for the Future (for humans and non-humans)
summary: The Oracle: Ritual for the Future is a 60-minute immersive performance by Victorine van Alphen (Studio Brave New Human) in which the audience moves through a 360-degree screen environment. Starting from the personal story and archival material of two AI enthusiasts, the audience is first given control and then overtaken by non-human entities and AI-generated images; in one scene, audience members who consented have their image altered by AI. It premiered at IDFA DocLab 2025.

title: The Power Loom
artist: Lesiba Mabitsela, Meghna Singh, Simon Wood
summary: The Power Loom is a multimedia installation that digitally weaves African textiles. It is one part of The Founders Pillars; the other part is a site-specific augmented reality experience that uses the same patterns to wrap the columns of the New York Stock Exchange as a memorial to enslaved peoples. It had its world premiere at Tribeca Immersive 2025 ('In Search of Us', WSA / Water Street Projects, 6–29 June 2025), and the project received a S+T+ARTS Prize Africa Award of Distinction in 2025.

title: The Quiet Weight of Shadows
summary: The Quiet Weight of Shadows is an installation shown at Aspinwall House in the Kochi-Muziris Biennale 2025-26 about the history of the ULFA insurgency in Assam. Visitors walk through a field of red- and green-lit artificial carnivorous plants that emit news broadcasts from the 1990s to 2010 in Assamese, Hindi and English, with watchtowers in which video interviews with former ULFA members play, and a reconstructed burnt house holding real archival newspapers, photographs, pamphlets and documents. The installation also screens the artist's film Whispers Beneath the Ashes (2025).

title: The Rift
summary: The Rift is a 6-minute 360° fulldome dance film shot in Zimbabwe, in which four dancers perform a shared choreography across forests, plains, urban settings and abandoned or painted buildings, with water as the unifying element. It was made by 4Pi Productions (Wales) with Matamba Film Labs and AfriKera Arts Trust (Harare) through the XR Labs collaboration.

title: The River is a Circle
summary: A software-driven generative animation made with James Schmitz and Blake Goble and shown on a large video wall on the Whitney Museum's fifth-floor terrace (Hyundai Terrace Commission, April 2025 – January 2026). It shows the Hudson River split between life above and below the water and changes by algorithmic probability with real-time weather, season, tides and marine traffic. title: The Teaching Tree

title: The Thinking Ocean
summary: The Thinking Ocean is an online interactive generative work commissioned by the Whitney Museum for its artport website, part of the artists' series Cosmosapience. Viewers move through a simulated underwater scene of particles and bubbles that turns into patterns resembling cells, circuitry and code, driven by motion-captured choreography, with a 20-minute audio loop of spoken-word poetry; touching the screen moves the view, and the webcam can bring the viewer's surroundings into the image. It runs in the browser (threejs, WebGPU), every open instance shares a synchronised palette and atmosphere, and it is also shown as an installation and a live performance.

quotes.text: The Thinking Ocean is a provocation to consider who and what we give personhood to, and why. quotes.text: Our biology was written in water. We crawled onto land, but we brought the ocean with us. We carry it inside us. What happens when we sever this connection? When we diminish these relationships, are we diminishing our own consciousness?

quotes.source: Project page, memo.tv

quotes.text: If computation is being taken as a criterion for ‘thinking,‘ or even ‘consciousness,’ then what natural systems might already qualify that we are overlooking? Why do we grant personhood to AI while denying it to natural systems like rivers, oceans, the atmosphere, and more?

title: They Who Saw Nothing but Beauty
summary: They Who Saw Nothing but Beauty is a series of seven jacquard-woven wool tapestries made during the artist's residency at the Jan van Eyck Academie and woven at the TextielLab of the TextielMuseum Tilburg. The compositions are drawn as pixel art in the software Aseprite and show scenes connected to the Battle of Karbala, including a two-faced figure based on Sayyida Zaynab, in dense black-and-white patterns drawn from southern Iraqi carpet-making and Shia iconography. The title refers to Zaynab's reply 'I saw nothing but beauty'; the work received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art + at Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

title: TOMORI

summary: A six-minute HD video performance in which the artist, wearing or pulling a long electric-blue fabric, moves through a forest towards a river and enters it, dragging the soaked fabric upstream until disappearing beneath a waterfall. title: Twin Quasar
summary: Twin Quasar is a three-dimensional virtual artwork and space in the Whitney Museum Virtual Landscape, commissioned for the Whitney's artport. It can be visited on the multi-user MONA platform, where visitors see and can talk to each other, and in the Apple Vision Pro.

title: Unknown Label
summary: Unknown Label is a single- or multi-channel video installation of about 16 minutes about online micro-workers in Venezuela, Kenya and the Philippines who outline and label images ("image segmentation") used to train self-driving cars for German and US car manufacturers. It combines the workers' testimonies with images they passed on and an animated digital collage of annotated images and a 3D map of the world as seen by self-driving cars, moving from single-colour segmentation to a city-scale 3D data visualisation. It was developed in 2023 during a European Media Art Platform residency at Werkleitz, received an Honorary Mention in New Animation Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2024, and was later released for cinema as Their Eyes (2025, with Lucas Azémar).

quotes.text: It is a video installation that deals with the human labour involved in training AI systems, and more specifically with the training of self-driving vehicles in order to "read" their environment, that is recognizing elements around a car when it's driving itself. The process is called "image segmentation" and it consists of drawing an outline around every object in a given image of a street and put a label on it. It is basically translating our world to be machine-readable.
quotes.speaker: Nicolas Gourault
quotes.source: In Dialogue: Artist Talk with werkleitz, EMAP / emare.eu

quotes.text: It was uncanny to discover this whole process of human labour which is hidden behind a cover of so-called intelligent algorithms. Far from the narrative of the technological breakthrough, there is still until now a very old school system that relies on the inequalities of the global economy in order to enable the AI systems that we benefit from in our daily lives.

quotes.source: In Dialogue: Artist Talk with werkleitz, EMAP / emare.eu

quotes.text: It was unsettling to hear the reflection of the workers upon images that to me seemed very familiar. quotes.text: It was important to build some trust with these people because everything is taking place online, there is a lot of fear about scam or abuse because the workers on this platform don't know their clients, they don't know who they're exactly working for. quotes.speaker: Nicolas Gourault
quotes.source: In Dialogue: Artist Talk with werkleitz, EMAP / emare.eu

quotes.text: Unknown Label reveals the hidden crowd that works with these operational images and help shape how machines see the world. A digital collage, layering together fragments of annotated images and a virtual map of the world as seen by self-driving cars, creates a space where the viewers can share the vision of otherwise invisible data workers. The video installation thus raises the question of how to reappropriate these operational images which depict and categorize the world we live in without our prior knowledge or agreement.

title: Void in Resonance
summary: Void in Resonance is a multi-channel film installation about El Campo Pesquero de Playa Bagdad, a community at the eastern end of the Mexico–U.S. border, four kilometres from SpaceX's spaceport in Boca Chica, Texas. It shows a SpaceX launch through the perspectives of people working in the oyster field, juxtaposing Playa Bagdad's vernacular architecture with elements evoking SpaceX designs in deliberately underexposed images. It was produced through the 2025 CIFO x Ars Electronica Award and premiered at Ars Electronica Festival 2025 (POSTCITY, Linz).

title: We Are Dead Animals
summary: We Are Dead Animals is a VR game, premiered at IDFA DocLab 2025, built from 3D scans (photograms) of dead animals the artist found in his surroundings, placed in a landscape that is his interpretation of paradise. Players fly through it with hand-tracking, revive animals, read about how they died, collect them, combine their body parts into new creatures, release them or eat them to extend a limited lifespan. At IDFA it was installed inside a nest built of organic material.

title: Where Do the Ants Go?
summary: A multiplayer video game installation inside a large walk-in sculpture of an anthill, designed with architect Jeremy Waterfield, in which visitors together steer a digital colony of programmed ants on screens around the interior. Players feed the colony with thoughts they type into the system, and depending on which thoughts are taken up the colony can burn, drown or starve; there is nothing to win or lose. It was first shown at Dhaka Art Summit 2023 and then travelled (Horst Arts and Music Festival, Zeppelin Museum, Pivô São Paulo), with the anthill rebuilt in local materials at each site.

title: Wisdoms for Love 3.0
artist: Keiken (with Obso1337, Ryan Vautier, Sakeema Crook)
summary: A decision-making web game and NFT project, also presented as an installation with an interactive fibreglass sculpture with LED lights and water fountains, controlled by iPad. Players move through a labyrinth of metaphorical decisions (the path of the Divine Mother, Human God or Moral High Horse), collect 'wisdom tokens' as free downloadable artworks with a 'moral contract', and can see other online players on a map. Iterations were shown at HEK / Transfer Gallery, the Thailand Biennale 2021, Gray Area Festival 2021 and SeMA Bunker, Seoul; it received an Honorary Mention in Computer Animation at Prix Ars Electronica 2022.

title: With the Heart Coming Out of the Mouth (Com o coração saindo pela boca)
summary: With the Heart Coming Out of the Mouth was Brazil's presentation at the 59th Venice Biennale (2022), curated by Jacopo Crivelli Visconti. Built on an index of more than 200 Brazilian idiomatic expressions that name body parts, it combines sculptures, photographs and a video; visitors enter through an outsized ear and leave through another, and at intervals a large fabric heart drops from a mouth in the ceiling and inflates to fill the second room. The expressions are captioned in Portuguese, English and Italian.

title: Without Us
summary: Without Us is a project by composer and percussionist Daniel Brandt made up of an album (Erased Tapes, March 2025), a 20-minute short film of the same name directed with Anthony Dickenson and shot in Athens in 2023, and a live performance in which the concert is interwoven with the film. The film follows Gaia, an Uber driver who decides humanity is the world's problem; the album uses field recordings including the hum of Europe's largest mall. The live A/V version premiered at the Barbican in London in April 2025 and was presented at CTM Festival 2026.

title: Zoom, Click, Waltz
summary: Zoom, Click, Waltz is a multimedia installation of 13 LED screens, each showing a person or people in a separate apartment window, dancing or not. It began during Singapore's 2020 Covid-19 'Circuit Breaker' lockdown, when the artist mailed letters to neighbours in her building asking them to dance by their living-room windows at a set time; the recordings are stitched together with staged, found and borrowed footage. It was shown at Gillman Barracks, Singapore (21 January - 7 February 2021) and won the 2021 Lumen Prize 3D/Interactive Award.
